## Course overview

A major challenge in creating reproducible computational outputs is the wide range
of systems research software may be expected to run on: hardware, operating
system and installed libraries can all vary from one machine to the next.
Containers address this problem by packaging an application together with
everything it needs to run into a reusable *image* that can be deployed in
a repeatable way across different systems.

This course teaches you to run, build and share container images using Podman with
Podman Desktop. By the end, you will be able to produce research software
outputs that are reproducible and FAIR (findable, accessible, interoperable and
reusable).

## Learning outcomes

By the end of this course, you will:

- Understand how disparate computing environments can make research software hard to build and reproduce
- Describe how containers provide a solution by running code and dependencies in a portable environment
- Be able to find, run and build container images using Podman Desktop
- Have published a container image for your own Python program to a public container registry
- Know how building, testing and publishing containers may be automated in development workflows
- Be ready to apply best practices for maintaining containers for research software 
- Recognise related tools, such as Podman Compose, Apptainer and Kubernetes, and when to use them

In order to follow the course, you will need to install Podman Desktop, as covered in [Module 0: Prerequisites](modules/00-prerequisites/index.qmd).

## Beyond the scope of this course

This course focuses on hands-on experience of running command-line and
web-based applications in containers using the Podman Desktop GUI. The
following topics are not covered in depth or at all:

- Using Podman or Docker from the command line
- Building and running containers with Apptainer
- Running graphical applications that do not have a web interface
- Multi-platform builds 
- Multi-container applications (Docker/Podman compose)
- GPU pass-through

Links to further resources will be provided when relevant for these
more advanced topics.  In particular, if you need to work on a HPC
cluster,  you will probably use Apptainer rather than
Podman. The [Apptainer User
Guide](https://apptainer.org/docs/user/main/introduction.html)
is a comprehensive reference.

## Relation to other Reproducible Research Cambridge (RRCam) courses

This course is the fourth in a series by the Reproducible Research Fellows Team:

Python → Git and Command Line → Testing → **Containers** → Kubernetes

As such, it may draw on some understanding from the previous courses, in
particular of basic Python and Shell (Bash). Module 3 will also make use of
GitHub Workflows, as introduced in the *Testing* course.  However, every case,
full code snippets and explanations will be provided for those not familiar with
these aspects.
